canonical_title: Lateral-directional control in dives and pullouts

versions.title_at_revision: Lateral-directional control in dives and pullouts
versions.text: Criterion: Verify that lateral-directional control in dives and pullouts is safe. Standard: The air vehicle meets the standards within MIL-STD-1797, 5.2.4.2 Lateral-directional control in dives and pullouts. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, simulation, and inspection of process, requirements, design, test, and configuration documentation. Additional References: 14 CFR 23.253 High speed characteristics 14 CFR 25.253 High-speed characteristics

versions.title_at_revision: Lateral-directional control in dives and pullouts
versions.text:
Standard: The roll and yaw control forces to maintain wings-level and zero sideslip, without retrimming, throughout dives and recoveries within the ROTH are no worse than the limits as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Lateral-Directional Control in Dives and Pullouts paragraph, unless pilot evaluation determines the air vehicle handling qualities are no worse than Level 2. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis and simulation to assess the roll and yaw control forces in dives and pullouts, including in the ROTH, as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Lateral-Directional Control in Dives and Pullouts paragraph for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess the roll and yaw control forces in dives and pullouts, including in the ROTH, as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Lateral- Directional Control in Dives and Pullouts paragraph for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess the roll and yaw control forces in dives and pullouts, including in the ROTH, as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Lateral-Directional Control in Dives and Pullouts paragraph for selected combinations of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions.
